draft.title: Health status across countries
card: Health status is how healthy a population is. It is often shown by life expectancy, child mortality and the main causes of death.
Life expectancy
the average number of years a newborn is expected to live. It is usually higher in high-income countries than in low-income countries.
Child mortality
the number of children who die before their fifth birthday, usually counted per 1000 live births. It is usually much higher in low- and middle-income countries.
Causes of death

In high-income countries, most deaths come from non-communicable diseases such as heart disease and cancer. In low-income countries, infectious diseases, such as pneumonia and diarrhoeal disease, cause a larger share of deaths.
draft.remember: Low-income countries tend to have lower life expectancy, higher child mortality and more deaths from infectious disease.

a.q: Which pattern in health status is most likely in a low-income country compared with a high-income country?
opts: Higher child mortality and lower life expectancy
Lower child mortality and higher life expectancy
Higher life expectancy and lower child mortality
Lower life expectancy and lower child mortality
a.why: Low-income countries tend to have more child deaths and shorter lives on average. The last option is tempting but mixes a low life expectancy with low child mortality, and the two usually move in opposite directions.
a.clue: Think about which measures usually worsen together.

b.q: In Country X, pneumonia and diarrhoeal disease cause many deaths. In Country Y, heart disease and cancer cause most deaths. What is the best conclusion?
opts: Country X is more likely to be low income than Country Y
Country Y is more likely to be low income than Country X
Both countries have the same level of income
Country Y has a higher child mortality rate than Country X
b.why: A larger share of deaths from infectious disease is typical of low-income countries. Heart disease and cancer are more common causes of death in high-income countries, so Country Y is not the likely low-income one.
b.clue: Which type of disease is linked with low-income countries?

a.best: Higher child mortality and lower life expectancy

b.best: Country X is more likely to be low income than Country Y

problems.detail: Why (a) calls the tempting option 'the last option' and describes it as low life expectancy with low child mortality. The options are shuffled, and that description matches 'Lower life expectancy and lower child mortality', not the last-listed option 'Higher life expectancy and lower child mortality'. The explanation should name the distractor by its content, not its position.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and each has one clear right answer. Why (a) refers to a distractor by position ('the last option'), which does not match the shuffled options and should name the option by its content.
